images.title: A diagonal makes two halves
images.purpose: Shows one diagonal cutting a 7 cm by 4 cm rectangle into two congruent triangles of 14 cm² each.
images.composition: One rectangle, large and centred, with one diagonal; the two triangles in two colours.
images.exact_structure: Plain white background, lots of empty space, the figure large and centred, thin dark outlines (#2B2B2B), flat fills. Only the labels listed appear; no other text, no scenery, no characters. A rectangle 7 units wide and 4 units tall, long side horizontal. A faint grey (#6B7280) grid of unit squares inside it: 7 columns and 4 rows, 28 unit squares. One diagonal drawn as a dark line from the bottom left corner to the top right corner. The lower right triangle is filled teal (#0072B2), the upper left triangle is filled amber (#E69F00), both semi light so the grid shows through. Labels: 7 cm under the bottom side, 4 cm beside the right side, 14 cm² inside the amber triangle near its centroid, 14 cm² inside the teal triangle near its centroid. Check: 7 × 4 = 28 and 28 ÷ 2 = 14.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: The diagonal cuts the rectangle into two equal triangles, each 14 cm².
images.description: Shows one diagonal cutting a 7 cm by 4 cm rectangle into two congruent triangles of 14 cm² each.
images.context: Matches the worked example: 7 cm by 4 cm rectangle, each triangle 14 cm².
images.teaching_notes: Ask the child to imagine turning the amber triangle round onto the teal one.

image_decisions.why: The halving is seen at a glance: two matching triangles inside one counted rectangle.
